note: Fast, narrow CME seen to the due east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2A, and GOES CCOR-1 likely associated with a destabilizing filament seen lifting off to the due east near N10E10 best seen in GOES SUVI 284 and GOES SUVI 304 around 2025-10-16T00:44Z.

note: Bright flux rope CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. The source is the combined effects of two eruptions from AR 14246 (N25W80) which occur in close succession. The first eruption from AR 14246 (N25W80) is characterized by a small loop of ejecta seen lifting off at or near AR 14246 (N25W80) starting at 2025-10-17T10:57Z in GOES SUVI 304 and very widely opening field lines from the same location seen in GOES SUVI 284. Brightening and opening field line movement can be seen from AR 14246 in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. The second eruption from AR 14246 (N25W80), which includes an M1.1 flare, is characterized by a much more rapid instance of opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting at 2025-10-17T12:37Z, and brightening and ejecta seen starting at 2025-10-17T12:45Z in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. Both instances of opening field lines likely resulted in two leading edges, which may have combined so early in their propagation that they appear as one leading edge by the time they appear in the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

The most likely candidate is some opening field lines from near the NW limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 and GOES SUVI 304 starting as early as 2025-10-20T01:30Z. The source of this event is field line opening and brightening seen in GOES SUVI 195 located at approx. N25E70 beginning at approx. 2025-10-20T02:36Z. This CME appears to be heavily deflected towards the North based on the source field lines and visual deflection as it propagates through the field-of-view in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME seen to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2. Not yet visible in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, or STEREO A COR2. Source is the eruption of a filament located on the far side of the Earth-facing disk. Filamentary material originating from just beyond the STEREO-A southwest limb (just beyond W139) can be seen lifting off from an apparent latitude of about S45, but with southern deflection as it erupts, in STEREO A EUVI 304 at about 2025-10-22T19:45Z. Filamentary material can also be seen emerging from beyond the South limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting at about 2025-10-22T20:01Z. As visual reference points on the Earth-facing disk, the filamentary material spans visually from about S50E70 to S55W60, but again, is actually located beyond the South limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very preliminary measurement of the leading edge based on careful approximation of where the center of the filament may be based on GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI imagery. This measurement is based on this approximation and the best fit using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 only.
Updated measurement of the leading edge using the two frames of STEREO A COR2 which have become available and several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3.

note: Wide CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured in real time by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2025-10-22T19:23Z. Source is likely an eruption from former AR 14246, estimated to be located at approx. N24W150. Brightening, a re-intensification of the nearly-continuous post-eruptive arcades, and opening field lines can be seen located at AR 14246 in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 in the 2025-10-22T19:35Z and 2025-10-22T19:45Z frames. A large rising loop and a few narrow pieces of ejecta can be faintly seen beyond the NW limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-10-22T21:39Z. A large rising loop from beyond the NW limb can be seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2025-10-22T21:13Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the SHOCK using the location of the candidate source seen in available UV imagery and best fit between a handful of frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured in real time by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2025-10-22T19:23Z.

Measurement of the BULK using the location of the candidate source seen in available UV imagery and best fit between a handful of frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured in real time by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2025-10-22T19:23Z.

note: Faint CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is partially obscured by Earth eclipse in GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely farsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEROE A COR2 in SWPC_CAT. The CME was not clearly measurable in GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery.

note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely an eruption seen near the limb in STEREO A EUV imagery from AR 14246, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2025-10-18. The eruption can be seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2025-10-23T04:54Z as opening field lines and post eruption arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. Not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap. Source is likely an eruption from AR 14246, located around longitude W150, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2025-10-18. The eruption can be seen near the limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2025-10-23T10:05Z as opening field lines and post eruption arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME visible to the SSE in STEREO A COR2 and the south of SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1. The potential source is either a filament eruption seen near the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery with liftoff starting around 2025-10-23T08:57Z or a filament eruption centered around S30W30 with liftoff starting around 2025-10-23T08:29Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using limited SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery due to the CME's faintness.

note: CME visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely an eruption from former AR 14246, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2025-10-18. Opening field lines and post eruption arcades are visible near the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2025-10-23T13:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement using early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT. The CME is not yet clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1.
Updated measurement with additional imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery and may be faintly visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. The source is speculative but may be related to an eruption from Active Region 14256 (S16W22) starting around 2025-10-23T15:45Z as seen in GOES SUVI 195/284/304 and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: This measurement is speculative as this event is difficult to observe in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery due to the faintness and overlapping material from preceding events. However, this measurement is based on the approximate source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery for a few frames before a data gap which begins at 2025-10-23T18:08Z. The source is an eruption from former Active Region 14248 (located around N07W130 at the time of the eruption) starting around 2025-10-23T16:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 and STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery. An opening of field lines is observed on the western limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery, while this same opening of field lines is observed from beyond the western limb in GOES SUVI 171, 195, and 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the north/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is only observed for a few frames in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap from 2025-10-23T18:08Z to 2025-10-23T20:53Z.The source is a large eruption from former AR 4246 (N25W157) starting around 2025-10-23T17:45Z seen from beyond the northwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery and GOES SUVI 284/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the brighter bulk feature based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

SHOCK measurement based on the source longitude. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, the shock front associated with this event is not seen in STEREO A. The measured parameters may vary as a result.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, starting with a half width less than 10 degrees but expanding to reach 10 degrees further in the field-of-view. The source is likely an area of brightening observed by STEREO A EUVI 195 around N12W60-N12W70 (as viewed by STEREO A) starting around 2025-10-24T01:30Z, also observed in GOES SUVI 284 over the NW limb as field line movement starting around 2025-10-24T02:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, although with some slight uncertainty due to the leading edge faintness in all coronagraph imagery. CME starts <10 degree half width but expands to fit in later imagery.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, not observed in GOES CCOR-1 due to an eclipse period, with a half width less than 10 degrees. The source is likely filament ejecta observed by STEREO A EUVI 304 around N12W60-N12W70 (as viewed by STEREO A) starting around 2025-10-24T03:50Z, better observed in GOES SUVI 284/304 over the NW limb as field line movement and filament ejecta starting around 2025-10-24T03:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, although with some slight uncertainty due to the leading edge faintness in all coronagraph imagery. CME <10 degree half width.

note: Faint CME to the E first observed in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, appears to develop within LASCO C3's field-of-view and is not observed in LASCO C2 or STEREO A COR2. No source is observed in available GOES SUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky with only SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 as these are the only two observing coronagraphs.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2, and GOES CCOR-1 for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. This event is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. The source is likely related to a filament eruption spanning S15E50 to S10E38 which begins to lift off around 2025-10-24T12:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. The filament is located between two coronal holes and the associated CME likely exhibits deflection to the east as a result.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The leading edge of this event becomes too diffuse to measure after a few frames. The measurement relies on early imagery as a result.

note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, with a notably faint/diffuse leading edge. The source may be field line movement observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 near the west limb as viewed from STEREO A beginning around 2025-10-24T12:55Z, also observed over the NW limb as viewed from GOES in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2025-10-24T13:17Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, with some uncertainty in parameters due to the faint, diffuse leading edge in all coronagraphs.

note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery, but becomes too diffuse to be observed in other coronagraphs. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement observed over the northwest limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery around 2025-10-24T18:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the uncertain/far-sided source location.

note: This CME is visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-10-24T18:08Z. The source is uncertain, but may be related to faint dimming centered near N50E20 seen in GOES SUVI 195 imagery starting around 2025-10-24T18:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the uncertain source location and data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event.

note: This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the south/southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint and narrow CME to the N in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. No source has been found and the CME is likely far-sided, possibly associated with the former AR 14246 which should be directly behind the Sun at the time.

Narrow CME to the SSW in SOHO LASCO and to the SSE in STEREO A coronagraphs. It is followed by a multitude of more minor fronts. Source might be a very minor filament eruption seen in GOES SUVI 195 to the S (~S37W05), also seen in STEREO A UVI 195 to the SE around 2025-10-25T07Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs and somewhat confirmed by the (very minor) potential source, a minor filament eruption.

note: Narrow CME to SSW in SOHO LASCO and to the SSE in STEREO A. The front looks wider in STEREO A and narrower in SOHO and GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs.

note: Wider CME following (and resembling) the 2025-10-25T06:36Z CME and directed S in all coronagraphs, with a multitude of follow up and preceding fainter fronts. No source has been found for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1).

note: Bright and wide far-sided partial halo CME seen to the NNW in STEREO A COR2 and as a N halo (slightly to the NNE) in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1, with a very wide shock and immediately following somewhat narrower bulk, possibly with two lobes. Its source is a significant restructuring of magnetic field far behind the NW limb seen in STEREO A EUV 195 at 2025-10-25T11:05Z (and possibly a minor ejecta from behind the NW limb seen in STEREO EUVI 304 at 2025-10-25T11:15Z. Coronal signatures are also more faintly seen in GOES SUVI 284 to the NNW as fast opening of field lines behind the limb after 2025-10-25T11:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) and confirming former AR 14246 located at -174 deg longitude at the time of eruption as the source.
The shock of this CME is not possible to fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 - or GOES CCOR-1 - and STEREO A COR2). Only a plane-of-sky analysis (with STEREO A COR2) is possible.

Updated SHOCK analysis triangulation between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1. Due to the oblong shape of the shock feature, the front does not fit well in all 3 coronagraphs together. STEREO A COR2 has the better viewing angle of the front with its spacecraft position around W49, so this fit focuses on capturing the full front in COR2A and fits most of the front, focusing on the eastern side, in LASCO C2/C3 and CCOR-1.

note: CME observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No clear source for this CME is observed, potentially some weak field line movement over the N limb in GOES SUVI 284 around 2025-10-25T17:01Z, and may be outflow from large far-sided CME 2025-10-25T11:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-10-26T02:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This event appears to be directed straight towards STEREO A, and is therefore not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this event is a small eruption from near AR 14256 (S16W56). Field line opening can be seen in GOES SUVI 195 beginning at approx. 2025-10-26T01:04Z, along with some dimming seen in STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: CME first seen to the North in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-10-26T08:36Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. There is no clear source seen for this event as it is likely far sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR and STEREO A COR2.
SHOCK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Narrow, faint CME with a messy unclear front, seen following the 2025-10-26T08:36Z CME (N in SOHO LASCO and as a NW jet in STEREO A COR2), and seen only in a few difference imagery timestamps of STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 before it dissipates. There is no clear source seen for this event as it is likely far sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1); with no support from the coronal signatures since the CME is clearly far-sided.

note: A faint, slow, loop partial halo (followed by another faint loop) CME seen in SOHO LASCO and CCOR-1 to the NE and not seen (covered by the large daily data gap) in STEREO A COR2. The start of this CME is likely earlier. No source has been found for it, so it is likely far-sided. The source could be former Active Region 14246, which should be at the longitude of -168 deg at the time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very speculative measurement with one coronagraph only (since STEREO A COR2 is not available because of the large data gap). The CME latitude could be different: the latitude of +24 deg has been selected as the latitude of the former AR 14246, however this AR has produced many CMEs with much higher latitude. As a result, latitude and speed of this event could be significantly different.

note: Faint northern partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, fully covered by a data gap in STEREO A.  No source has been found for this CME in available EUV imagery, so it is likely far sided, possibly from the former AR 14246 which should have the longitude of ~ -165 deg.

cmeAnalyses.note: A rather speculative one-coronagraph (LASCO) analysis because the CME is not seen in STEREO coronagraph due to a large data gap. The latitude (and hence the speed) could be different. The latitude of 24 deg is chosen to correspond to the latitude of former AR 14246 when it was seen on the front side. The Active Region produced multiple more northern CMEs, so this analysis is very approximate.
Very approximate, uncertain one-coronagraph measurement of a fainter wider shock.

note: Partial halo half-loop to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, overlapping with the 2025-10-26T20:36Z northern brighter halo CME. Fully covered by a large daily data gap in STEREO A. Its source was not found, so is likely far-sided. The former AR 4246 should be at -165 deg long at the time, however the latitude of this CME is lower than the 24 degrees of this AR.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate one coronagraph analysis (SOHO) due to data gap in STEREO A and likely far-sidedness of this CME.
